title: A family of closed subsets of a quasi-compact space with the finite intersection property has nonempty intersection

standard_prerequisites.name: The definition of quasi-compactness through the finite-subcover property of open coverings, and the complementation correspondence between open and closed subsets
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the author's section on quasi-compact spaces and maps, immediately before the counted statement
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the reformulation of the statement that the proof argues by contraposition.

core_obligations: Contraposition: the proof assumes the intersection of the closed subsets to be empty, which by complementation turns the family of complements into an open covering of the space (proof lines 1949-1952).

Finite subcover: quasi-compactness extracts from that covering a finite subcover, and complementing back gives that the intersection of the corresponding finitely many closed subsets is empty (proof lines 1952-1958).
The hypothesis contradicted: the finite intersection property assumed in the statement is violated, so the assumption fails and the intersection is non-empty (proof lines 1958-1960).
Conclusion: the finite intersection property implies non-emptiness of the whole intersection (proof lines 1960-1961).
proof_roadmap: 反证中取补：交集为空 ⇔ 开集族覆盖 X。
由准紧性取出有限子覆盖，补回来即得有限多个 Z_α 交集为空，与题设的有限交性质矛盾。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the finite-intersection form of quasi-compactness (author lemma at source lines 1940-1946, label lemma-intersection-closed-in-quasi-compact). The proof (source lines 1948-1961) is a clean contraposition: emptiness of the intersection becomes an open covering after complementation (proof lines 1949-1952), quasi-compactness yields a finite subcover, and complementing that subcover back produces a finite subfamily with empty intersection, contradicting the hypothesis (proof lines 1952-1960). The reformulation is used repeatedly later in the chapter, in particular for the spectral-space material. H2.
